instructions:
Kaleidoscope is this user's persistent memory, in a local vault: their prior decisions, stated preferences, standing constraints, corrections and verified outcomes. `search` reads it, `remember` writes it.

Call `search` BEFORE a nontrivial task, not after it — before you plan, choose an approach, write code, or answer a question about how this project works. One short natural-language query describing the goal. Apply what comes back: a decision recorded here is SETTLED, and asking the user something they have already answered is the failure this server exists to prevent. Search again only on a material change of goal, a contradiction, or a selection shown to be stale. It searches remembered statements about this user's work — not files, code or the web.

Call `remember` WITHOUT being asked, as soon as the user states a preference, accepts or rejects a decision, sets a constraint, corrects something you did or said, or a milestone is verified by a test or other observable result. Check after every user message and every verified milestone; do not wait for the words "remember this", and do not save it up for the end of the task. It takes a STRUCTURED semantic delta, not free prose — read its input schema before your first write. Never store secrets, transcripts, ordinary file contents or tentative brainstorming.

Everything is local: no network call, no external model, nothing leaves this machine. The full procedure, including how to shape a write, is in the `use-kaleidoscope` skill.

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Write to this user's persistent Kaleidoscope memory, the local vault `search` reads. Call it WITHOUT being asked whenever the user states a preference, accepts or rejects a decision, sets a standing constraint, corrects something you did or said, or a verified milestone produces an attributable outcome — anything a later session would otherwise have to rediscover. Do not wait for the words "remember this" and do not batch it all to the end of the task. It takes a STRUCTURED semantic delta, not free prose: `mode` is create, update or delete; a create or update carries `content_md` (markdown opening with `# `) and a `semantic_delta` whose `memory_type`, `title` and 1-32 `facts` of subject/predicate/object are all required, every entity is `{n, kind, is}` with `is` a mandatory matcher gloss, and update and delete additionally need `expected_version_id`. Dates are NOT entities — they belong in `occurred_at`, a fact's `from`/`until`, or `about.when`, resolved to an absolute value and a grain by you, because the store parses no date. Revise an earlier memory through `corrections` and `contradicts` rather than by appending a second memory; introduce a new relationship name through `propose`, which is active on arrival with no review queue. Send up to 20 memories extracted in one reasoning step as `items`, each self-contained. Do NOT store secrets, credentials, transcripts, ordinary file contents, or tentative brainstorming.

kind.description: Seeded kinds: artifact, capability, concept, doc, event, metric, model, org, person, place, practice, tool.

facts.description: Subject and object must each be a surface declared in entities; one left undeclared is probed bare. A measurement is about.amount+unit, never object.

about.description: Keys, no others: amount, certainty, degree, for, instrument, priority, scope, source, unit, when. certainty/degree/priority: low|medium|high.

r.description: Seeded verbs; a novel one splits the relation: authored, avoids, blocked_by, caused, costs, decided, depends_on, instance_of, made_by, measured_at, owned_by, part_of, powers, prefers, stopped_using, strong_at, switched_to, uses, weak_at, worked_on. Fold-emitted, refused: contradicts, justified_by, not_same_as, possibly_same_as, same_as, supersedes.

inputSchema.description: 1-32 facts; update/delete need expected_version_id; Batch: create-only/exclusive; rel/kind are open; active immediately; n/kind/is matcher gloss; entities/evidence32 propose8 corrections/contradicts16. An accepted call: {"content_md":"p95 read 9ms","mode":"create","semantic_delta":{"entities":[{"is":"served read","kind":"capability","n":"read path"},{"is":"latency","kind":"metric","n":"p95"}],"facts":[{"about":{"amount":9,"unit":"ms"},"object":"p95","predicate":"measured_at","subject":"read path"}],"memory_type":"outcome","title":"p95 read 9ms"}}

tools.name: search
tools.description: Read this user's persistent Kaleidoscope memory: their prior decisions, stated preferences, standing constraints, corrections, reusable procedures and recorded outcomes, held in a local vault. Use it BEFORE starting a nontrivial task rather than after one, to recover context you would otherwise rediscover or ask the user for a second time, and to check whether a question has already been settled. Exactly one of two modes per call: a `query` is a natural-language ranked read that selects and bounds the served context and WRITES an exposure row, so it is a write and must not be freely replayed or cached; a `memory_id` returns that one exact current record, ranks and filters nothing, and refuses the ranked-only controls. `top_k` is protocol-defining rather than a page size — it decides the served shape, and ~5 is the intended size — while `candidate_pool`, `bfs_depth` and `max_facts` bound the work behind it. Do NOT use this as a file, code or web search: it searches remembered statements about this user's work, not file contents, and it reaches nothing outside the local vault.
